cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the Ganga kings and the lengths of their reigns down to Anantavarman and mentions that his coronation was celebrated on Saturday, śukla-pakshatritīyā, Revatī, in the month Kumbhu of the Śaka year 999, states that since Mundaparu which had been originally granted to brahmans along with the village of Khonna in the Varshavardhani-vishaya by the king's grandmother, Janakadēvī in the Śaka 1003 was subsequently reunited with the village of Gara, eighty-eight vrittis of land were taken over in return for it from the village of Talupu and granted by the king to the brahmans as compensation.

cells.remarks: Gives the usual genealogy of the Eastern Chalukyas down to king Vijayāditya. Registers the grant, in the presence of the assembly of Mahājanas, free of all taxes and imposts, to the Vedic scholar Pampanārya-Bhaṭṭopādhyāya of the Parāśara-gotra for the merit, prosperity and health of the king. The donee and his ancestors are praised for their scholarship. The inscription was composed by the poet Mutteya-Bhaṭṭa and inscribed on the plates by Paṭṭala. The grant is addressed to the Kuṭumbis (householders) of Gudda-vāj-vishaya.

cells.date: Śaka 1361, Siddhārthi, Jyeṣhṭha śu. pañchami, Saturday, Tīsday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant by the king, of twenty-four villages in the Gangamēda (i.e. Gedag country) which comprised 60 villages and which was situated in Tōragallu-nāḍu in Lakkonḍu-venthe, a subdivision of Poin.a-Hastināvatī (i.e. Hampe) to the gurus Tryambaka and Vīranārāyaṇa at Gadag at the instance of Vāṇīvilāsa Śrī-Kriyāśakti-guru. The control and management of the two temples was entrusted to Tryambaka who was a brāhmaṇa of the Kauśika-gotra and Bodhāyana-sūtra and who was the rājādhyaksha (accounts officer) of the Gadag-dēśa.

cells.date: Kali 4834, Śaka 1657 (wrongly cited for 1655), Pramādi, Āḍi 23, Friday, saptami, Ut-tiraṭṭādi.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant, of the magamai duties levied on articles of merchandise like yarn, tobacco, areca-nut, pepper, sandalwood, etc., to the temple of Puṇṇalai-vēlayudhasvāmi in the Kongu country, by the representatives of the 24 countries and Paṭṭaṇakkāras assembled together, for offerings and worship to the god while Kumāra-Dēvappayyan was administering the Kōyambuttur-sīmai as the agent of Sikkhanyarāvayyan Chkkarāja] who was the executive officer of the king. The entire management of the charity was left in charge of Periya-nambi of the Tiruvāvādurai-matham. Mentions Kapparāvaļ Narasingarāja-Uḍaiyar as the ancestor of the king.

Refers to the ruin of villages in the year of Periyāḷvār in Kuḷattūr, in the Chōḷa country, due to the insufficiency of cultivable lands, as a consequence of which the villages were abandoned by the people, and to their subsequent rehabilitation in the third year of Rājarāja (III?).

cells.date: 30th year (3rd day, and 24th year, Dhanus, śu. ekādaśī, Anīlam, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 79: 24th year, Dhanus, ba. chaturdaśī, Aṇilam, Monday = A.D. 1203, December 8, Wednesday ; f.d.t. ·18; ·43. The week-day quoted in the inscription is probably a mistake for Wednesday.]
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the lands added to the temple as tirumattak-kāṇi till the 20th year of the king. Records a sale as (Subhavēḷai) to the temple by the assembly of Tiruvāḷundūr, a brāhmaḍēya in Tiruvāḷundūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Vīra-Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, of land belonging to two individuals named Kaviṇiyan Śrīkaṇṭhan and Peri-yaṇḍār for 1,060 kāśu, in pursuance of the royal order confiscating the lands of those mischievous people who were a source of trouble the brahmans, Vēḷḷāḷas and to the temple. Mentions the (Vishnu) temple of Tiruk-kaḍavai-Āḷvār in the village.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction திருமா வளர etc. Records an agreement by the assembly of Ilachchikkudi alias Vikramachōḷachaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadeya in Rājēndra-śiṅga-vaḷanāḍu, a subdivision of Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, to pay the taxes levied, in the land-survey made by order of the king, on the lands belonging to the temple of Tiruvāduturai-udaiya-Paramasvāmi at Sattanūr a brahmadeya in Tiruvalundur-nāḍu, in payment of the interest on the money which they had received some time previously from the temple but which they were unable to pay back. In continuation of this is another inscription of the 26th year of the same king recording a gift of land in Ilangaikkudi in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu a sub-division of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu, for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple.

The nakshatra ‘Uttiram’ quoted in the inscription is evidently a mistake for ‘Hasta’, which was current till ‘81 on Sunday. śu. saptami ended at ‘65 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction திருமா வளர etc. Registers a sale of land to the temple, made tax-free, by the assembly of Abhayāśrayach-chaturvēdimangalam alias Sattanūr, a brahmadeya in Tiruvalundur-nāḍu, a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu. Mentions the hall called Ulagalandān to the north of the temple, where the assembly met and made the sale. The land is in the 5th year of the king by the residents (ūrōm) of Kīlūr in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu for burning a perpetual lamp before the god.

Gives the list, with their situation and extent, of the dēvadāna lands of the big temple at Talaichchāngādu in Akkur-nādu, a sub-division of Jayangondasōla-valanādu as entered in the register. Mentions a land called 'Immadiśōla-mādēviyāgam' belonging to the dēvadāna of the same temple. Records the change of a vēlī of dēvadāna land into tirundā-mattu[k]kāni owing to the failure of the tenant to pay the annual due of paddy on the land consecutively and the subsequent resumption of the same by the assembly. The tenant's consent was obtained for the forfeiture and the land was let out on lease (அடைக்கலப் பட்டது) to the tenants, with the sanction of the assembly.

cells.location: Bennakal
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Kaleśvara temple
cells.king: Pratāpachakravartin Vīra-Narasimhadēva, 'ruling from his capital Dōrasamudra.'
cells.date: Śaka 1148, [Vyaya], Chaitra, Sura, Sunday, Uttarā-yaṇa-Samkrāmi, Vyatīpata.
cells.remarks: Extols the Hoysoļa dynasty and traces its descent from Sula. Sodanda-Dandanayaka, the Pradhane (chief Minister) Amityo-Dandanayaka of Hoysala King Pratapa-Kava-naraya, constructed the temples of Kamyēśvara, Ampritesvara, Lakshmi-Narayana, Vanōdēvara, Ballalēśvara and Narasimha at Bennakullu, the chief town of the sub-division Boppanahalli-Twelve situated in the Kōgali 500 province which formed part of the Noṇambavādi-nādu, and that he made grants of land in several villages for its worship, maintenance and repairs. The grants are said to have been made by him in the presence of the gods Vajrēśvara and Sōmanathevada after washing the feet of the (Saiva) teacher Kaléśvaradēva who is called here the Rājaguru (royal preceptor).

Sodanda-Dandanayaka, the Pradhane (chief Minister) Amityo-Dandanayaka of Hoysala King Pratapa-Kava-naraya, constructed the temples of Kamyēśvara, Ampritesvara, Lakshmi-Narayana, Vanōdēvara, Ballalēśvara and Narasimha at Bennakullu, the chief town of the sub-division Boppanahalli-Twelve situated in the Kōgali 500 province which formed part of the Noṇambavādi-nādu, and that he made grants of land in several villages for its worship, maintenance and repairs. The grants are said to have been made by him in the presence of the gods Vajrēśvara and Sōmanathevada after washing the feet of the (Saiva) teacher Kaléśvaradēva who is called here the Rājaguru (royal preceptor).Read more (1 KB)

cells.place: On another rock in the field at Vallimōḍu Pettai. †
cells.remarks: Stones lost. Begins with the introduction ஶ்ரீமத்... . Records a gift of 32 cows for the perpetual lamp in the temple of Rōjartjēśvaram-uḍaiya-Mahādēva at Maḍavilāgam-apuram in Taṇḍarai-nāḍu, a sub-division of Yōdhirājakula-vaḷanāḍu, by a certain Paḷḷi-Tiṇḍivanam, an archer of the king's army, residing in the town, in expiation of his having killed his companion by mistake in a hunt. On the west wall of the same shrine is a modern inscription dated in Kali 4994 (=A.D. 1892-93) Nandana, Tai 19, Monday, stating that the repairs to the temple were commenced on this date. Records an agreement to pay a paṇam every month on each loom, by the weavers of the village, for the encouragement given to them to re-settle in the village, by the late Ōyma-Nāyakkār, an agent of Vaḷu-Nāyakkār in Nagamu-Nāyakkār-nallūr, they having owing to bad times they had emigrated to other places.

cells.place: On the walls of the deserted temple near the Sarvattham tank at Big Conjeeveram, Conjeeveram taluk, Chingleput district.
cells.remarks: Stones out of order. Seems to record the royal grant of a 1a-free village named Sarvarththa-nallūr in Kayirampōḍu-nāḍu, a division of Vīravīra-kōṭṭam in Jayangoṇḍa-śōḷa-maṇḍalam, for the various expenses of worship and offerings in the temple of Sarvārththa-uśaiya-Nāyaṉār made by the residents of the temple of the king while he was seated on his throne called Pallavarājaṉ (¹) in the outer hall (śīlai-maṇḍapam) Rājādhirājaṉ, in his palace at Gaṅgaikoṇḍaśōḷapuram. All the inscription are mixed up pieces of another inscription belonging to the same king which begins with the introduction திங்களூர் மலர்ந்‌து etc.
